papers.title: Image Processing Methods Based on Key Temperature Features for State Analysis and Process Monitoring of Selective Laser Melting (SLM)
papers.abstract: Selective laser melting (SLM) is a kind of additive manufacturing where parts are made directly from 3D CAD data layer-by-layer from powder material. Process monitoring is significantly important for quality control and assurance. A large number of studies have shown that the forming process temperature is closely related with the process state, and has influence on the final quality of the built part. On-line temperature measurement can generate a large number of real-time data of the dynamic temperature field, which facilitates the deployments of big data technologies for state analysis and process monitoring of the SLM process. In this paper, the concept of key temperature feature is proposed based on the characteristics of the dynamic temperature field, to guide the feature extracting from original image of the temperature field, as well as an automatic feature extracting method for image processing; then, the data structure of the key temperature features is constructed to store the pre-treated data, and provide database for subsequent data mining. Finally, the experiments of data collecting and image processing are carried out to verify the feasibility of the proposed method.

summary_en.motivation: To ensure quality in selective laser melting, real-time monitoring of the temperature field is essential for process state analysis.
summary_en.method: The concept of key temperature features is introduced, and an automatic feature extraction method via image processing is developed, with a structured database for subsequent data mining.
summary_en.result: Experimental data collection and image processing confirm the feasibility of the proposed method for SLM process monitoring.
summary_en.validation: Feasibility is validated through actual SLM experiments involving temperature field data acquisition and image processing.
